text: In this world, everyone lives on a train that never stops. See, a hundred years ago, the entire planet froze, and the last survivors were forced to live on a train with one thousand carriages. The government says it's minus eighty degrees outside, and if the train ever stops, we all die. But not everyone lives the same way. The rich live at the front with swimming pools, restaurants, and even private gardens. The workers live in the middle, keeping the train running. And the poor? We live in the very last carriages. My name is Logan, and I've never seen the outside world. Every day, we get one tiny portion of food. But one morning, the guards tell my mom there's nothing left. She hasn't eaten in two days, and I can't just watch her starve. So that night, I sneak into a maintenance tunnel. It leads straight toward the front of the train. I crawl through the darkness until I reach the workers' section. Then I keep going, and what I see next makes me furious. The rich are eating enormous meals. They're throwing away more food than my entire carriage gets in a week. I grab a bag of supplies for my mom, but just as I'm about to leave, a guard spots me. Hey, stop right there. I run through the carriages, past restaurants, swimming pools, and even a giant indoor garden until I finally reach the engine room, and that's when I notice something strange. A screen shows a live camera feed from outside, but there's no snow, no ice, just green forests, rivers, and actual people. The world has been safe for years. Suddenly, the train's commander walks in. He tells me the truth. The rich kept the train moving because they didn't wanna lose their power. Then he reaches for the alarm, but I'm faster. I pull the emergency brake. The entire train begins to shake. For the first time in a hundred years, it stops. The doors slowly open. Warm sunlight fills the carriages. I run back and help my mom outside. She kneels down and touches a real flower. Then she looks at me and smiles. I thought I'd never see the sun again. And for the first time in our lives, we're finally free.
